newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage company eyes O.J. Simpson home - report.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage company eyes O.J. Simpson home - report.

text.p: A mortgage company has started foreclosure proceedings against O.J. Simpson because he has missed $86,000 in payments on his Los Angeles mansion, the New York Post reported Friday.

By California law, Simpson has three months in which to pay the money he owes to Hawthorne Savings, which financed the house, the report said. If he does not pay, the company has the right to sell the property at an advertised public auction.

Former football star Simpson was cleared in criminal court in 1995 on charges of stabbing to death his former wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ronald Goldman in Los Angeles in June 1994. But he was held liable for the deaths in civil court this year.
The selling of the mansion in Brentwood, Los Angeles would be complicated by the $19 million lien that Ron Goldman's father has filed against Simpson's home.

Fred Goldman, who pursued the case against Simpson in civil court after his acquittal on criminal charges, wants any money from the sale of the house to go toward the $19 million a civil jury awarded him in damages after finding that Simpson was responsible for the deaths.
Goldman's lawyer Peter Gelblum was quoted by the New York Post as saying the mortgage company would have first option on the Brentwood estate.

A review of court records showed Goldman was about 10th in line of creditors to whom Simpson was indebted, the newspaper said. The list includes the attorneys who represented Simpson in both the criminal and civil trials.
